title: The Value of Patient-Reported Outcomes for Improving Care in Persistent Somatic Symptoms (PSS): The PSS Use Case of the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research within the German Medical Informatics Initiative (PCOR-MII)
summary:
This study is part of a larger project called Patient‑Centered Outcomes Research within the Medical Informatics Initiative (PCOR‑MII). The aim of PCOR‑MII is to systematically integrate information that patients report about their own health into routine medical care and link it with other medical data. This allows patients’ experiences to be better used to improve healthcare.

In the present study, we focus on people with persistent physical symptoms. Many people experience symptoms such as pain, fatigue, or gastrointestinal problems over several months without a clear medical explanation. These symptoms can strongly affect daily life and often occur together with stress, anxiety, or depressive symptoms.

All participating patients complete regular questionnaires about their symptoms, mood, quality of life, and daily functioning. These questionnaires are completed on site at the start of treatment and then remote every three months over a two-year period. The responses are collected in a digital platform that helps track the course of symptoms and adjust treatment accordingly.

The aim of the study is to improve understanding of persistent physical symptoms, tailor treatment more closely to the individual needs of patients, and develop new approaches to improve healthcare in the long term.

interventions.name: Longitudinal, multicenter observational study in patients with persistent somatic symptoms (PSS) within routine clinical care. No study-specific intervention is performed. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who present themselves at one of the participating clinics, have a PHQ-15 sum-score at intake of >= 10, and provide broad consent for the use of their routine clinical data
Exclusion criteria:
none
